Members of the collegium had previously analysed some documents, some attachments to the plan, gave their suggestions, opinions, before the Chief of General Staff actually approved the decision. When the army commander justified, explained, his decision, then it was signed and approved by the Chief of General Staff, which meant that the decision was approved and it could then be implemented.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at Exhibit 3D757, page 1 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, are you familiar with this document that is called: "Threat to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and ability of the Yugoslav Army to offer resistance," report of the Chief of General Staff of the Yugoslav Army?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: What were the circumstances in which this document was drafted?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Let me now go back a little bit before I comment on this document. In early August, you saw that on the 3rd the directive was already at the 3rd Army command and the plan of use was already approved for them. In mid-August, the Chief of General Staff with a team of people, his associates, assistant chiefs, went to visit the 3rd Army, paying special attention to the Pristina Corps, in order to analyse the overall situation in the units, to see what assistance should be given, to solve some problems, to see the requests submitted by the subordinate commands, and on the basis of the overall situation and the reports that we in the General Staff received from the subordinate army commands, this analysis was drafted at the level of the General Staff. The purpose was for the Chief of General Staff to inform the Supreme Defence Council and the country leaders with the situation in the army with the special emphasis on the tasks that were carried out at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Who took part in the elaboration of this document?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: As for the elaboration of this document, in the overall assessments -- well, I would say that all sectors and administrations in the General Staff participated because this was a complex analysis that was used to assess the overall situation and to present it to the top authority of the country, what the situation was like and what it was dealing with, what the army was dealing with, and also what should be done in the future period.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, that was at the time when NATO was threatening to intervene militarily, am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I said that in the General Staff as a whole situations were followed on a daily basis, in the country and outside the country. The situation in the army was also assessed and there were reliable indicators to the effect that there could be an aggression in that period of time, that is to say the autumn of 1998. Therefore, the objective was to carry out this analysis, to make this assessment in order to take timely measures for tasks to be implemented in the newly created situation that could be imposed on us.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the English text, page 5 of this same document, and of course the appropriate text in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, I would like to draw your attention to a paragraph that is the third one in the English version that says: "The army of Yugoslavia completed all its tasks fully and professionally and played the main role in operations against sabotage groups, thus having a decisive influence on the positive outcome of those operations." This is a document that was signed by the Chief of General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia and that was presented by the Chief of General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia. Did he really believe that at that period of time the Army of Yugoslavia completed all its tasks fully and professionally?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: What is presented here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I don't know where the question is going, but the way it's formulated asks the witness to engage in some sort of reading of the mind of the Chief of General Staff. He could probably speak about what indications there were or something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There's a lack of any foundation at the moment for asking beyond the question you already had answered: What does the document say?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Perisic was Chief of General Staff at that time, am I right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, General Perisic was Chief of General Staff at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown this same document page 7 in B/C/S, paragraph 6 on that page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: You see it. Now, tell me the following, General. In this document -- it's just disappeared, hasn't it, but I'm going to read it. Paragraph 6 says: "The General Staff of the VJ mainly focused on performing tasks of the Pristina Corps and took measures of full and good-quality replenishment of the corps with manpower and materiel. The command was guided in its work by regular and interim controls, and we assisted the Pristina Corps in performing the received tasks." Can you give us your comment on this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: As for the function of command in addition to issuing orders there is another element and that is control, checks. And the objective of that is to check how a task is being implemented and to see what the actual situation was within units, also to give help to subordinate commands, and to help resolve problems that the said unit has.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, sorry. Could you tell us in this particular case, what could this conclusion really apply to?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: The Chief of General Staff directly took a team to check the Pristina Corps in mid-August 1998, and that that was one of the principle tasks for the organs from the General Staff. As you can see, the Chief of General Staff assessed that it was indispensable for him to be on the spot with his associates on the basis of information, briefings, and concrete insight into the situation. On the basis of all of that, he would be able to take further measures down the chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, were you together with General Perisic when he went out to check what the situation is?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was there for that check, or rather, for that team that was headed by the Chief of General Staff, among others from other sectors and organs, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, because of the time that we have available, we don't want to go into detail, but as for this document 3D757, we would like to have it examined in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, now we're going to move on to what happened somewhat later after the date of this document, that is, and these were the talks between General Perisic and General Clark. You were a participant in the delegation that took part in the negotiations?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was one of the members of the collegium of the Chief of General Staff who attended the talks between General Perisic, Chief of General Staff; and General Clark.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Where were these negotiations held?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: These negotiations or talks were held on the premises of the General Staff where the General Staff had been deployed before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Who attended, General?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean totally or only from the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I mean only from the General Staff, and then you can tell us about everybody else.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I remember the meeting very well. As for the state organs, the president of the Republic of Serbia, Mr. Milutinovic, attended; as well as Mr. Sainovic; then the minister, the then-foreign minister, Mr. Jovanovic; from the General Staff in addition to General Perisic, the Chief of the General Staff; the head of the security administration, General Dimitrijevic was there; then I was there as assistant chief; then General Panic as the KLV assistant; and then the chef de cabinet, Colonel Vlajkovic; and also in attendance were representatives of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia, as far as I remember, General Djordjevic, General Lukic, and General Obrad Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: How long did the negotiations last?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: These negotiations started sometime in the evening. There were a few breaks and they went on until the morning hours if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Actually, I didn't ask you when it was that the talks were held.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: The negotiations were held on the 25th of October, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were these negotiations brought to a successful conclusion?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: If I can put it this way, it was a rather complex discussion, and I think that ultimately with the participation of all on both sides, they were concluded successfully.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Briefly, what was the result of these negotiations?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was the time when the agreement on the missions, on the OSCE and NATO missions in Kosovo and Metohija, had already been signed. After the well-known negotiations between President Milosevic and Holbrooke, the focus was on what the tasks were, if I can put it that way, of the state and of the army that were derived from these negotiations, or rather, this agreement on the establishment of OSCE and NATO missions in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: In relation to the army, tell me what was the result of these negotiations?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: We were most interested in the part of the agreement that pertained to the army. I'm saying that because I was present there. That is to say, if I can put it this way, as for the overall volume of work there, what was it that applied to the army, what were the tasks of the army as a whole, what were the tasks of the General Staff, and what should be done in order to embark on the realisation of the attained agreement and to take upon obligations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: What were the obligations taken upon by the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: The Chief of General Staff before this meeting when the agreement was signed -- there were actually discussions at the collegium --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, General, let's not go into all that detail. What was the result of the negotiations? What were the obligations of the Army of Yugoslavia on the basis of these negotiations?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: One of the tasks was for the units primarily of the Pristina Corps to be returned to barracks. It was agreed that they would remain within the territory, a few company-rank units would remain, as we called it then; also to fully honour the obligations we had vis-a-vis the verification mission, and also what the state took upon itself as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With relation to the withdrawal of the army, or rather, these units that stayed behind in the territory, did General Perisic have any comments in this regard and did he tell the other side what that was?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: In a way, I was in favour of looking at what the essence was of leaving such units within the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, General, sorry, I asked you whether General Perisic had --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I understood your question. I'll answer. General Perisic accepted what had been discussed until then, but noting that if the other side does not observe the agreement and if the external factor does not exercise its influence over the other side, that he would be compelled to return units within the territory from which they had withdrawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: What was the reaction of the other side, the representative of -- representatives of NATO, General Clark and General Naumann?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: They promised that that would be carried through; however, time quickly showed that that was not fully the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, let's go back to a document from a few days before that, before these negotiations started, that is, 3D645.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see the English text, page 5 -- [In English] I'm sorry. [Interpretation] Page 2 of the English text.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, this is what General Perisic said. Would you please focus on this, on the part -- actually, this is the collegium from the 23rd of October, that is to say, three days before the negotiations. Could you give us your comments as to these remarks of General Perisic's.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: These were the three units that had remained in the area. I don't have to go into all of that. One at Dulje, one at Lapusnik, and one at Klina near Pec.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom in on paragraph 3 in English and in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, could you please concentrate on this unit that stayed behind that was in the area, in the area of Podujevo. Can you give us your comments on this part?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I can, I can. In addition to these three units that I referred to, there was one company-strength unit in the area of Podujevo. In the talks that General Perisic had at that time there were some objections as to whether the time was right for that unit to be there; however, quite a few circumstances showed that this unit was there for training. At that time, we had these young soldiers who had come --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, sorry for interrupting but could you please look at paragraph 3, the 23rd of October, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Four units in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: That's right, and now this part that pertains to the unit in Podujevo, that -- that's the next segment.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the terrorist forces were trying to cut this road in order to make it impossible for our units to manoeuvre along this axis because there were quite a few indicators to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In this text General Perisic notes that a concession might be made by pulling this unit out. Can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, people were thinking along those lines, that this unit might be pulled out in order for them purportedly to exert pressure on the other side, to cease and desist on some activities that they were engaged in at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like page 4 of the English version to be brought up on the screen. Could we now please focus or zoom in on General Ojdanic's intervention.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, you will see the Serbian version momentarily. Could you please look at this document, in particular paragraph 2 in General Ojdanic's remarks, and I would like you to comment on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: B/C/S text page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So could you please look -- could you please comment on the entire intervention of General Ojdanic at this meeting of the collegium two days before the negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: General Ojdanic was the assistant Chief of General Staff at that time, and in this capacity he expressed a certain dilemma that actually was at odds with the current decision --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: What was the dilemma faced by General Ojdanic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in essence he wanted the remaining units, if I may call them that, the combat groups, to be withdrawn back to the barracks or to be deployed closer to the border in order to be able to intervene if -- if any serious problems at the border occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please now be shown Exhibit 3D646, page 9 in the English version paragraphs 3 and 4. That's the collegium of the 26th of October. It should be the collegium of the 26th of October, 1998. 3D646, I don't think that we have the right document on the screen. It's okay now. Page 9 of the English version, paragraphs 3 and 4. [In English] Page 9 English version, B/C/S version page 13. English version is okay now and the B/C/S ...

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, we're waiting for the English version to come up, but this is the collegium of the 26th --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The English is there, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour, it's my mistake. [Interpretation] We're waiting for the Serbian version to come up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, you will see in front of you the intervention by General Dimitrijevic at the collegium of the 26th of October, 1998, and I would like to ask you in the context of this debate at the collegium of the 23rd of October and debate at the negotiations on the 25th of October, could you please comment --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Page in B/C/S, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: -- [Interpretation] To comment on what General Dimitrijevic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Now it's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, you can't see his name, but the first two passages are, in fact, what he said, what General Dimitrijevic said. It is quite clear. So the first two passages on the page that you see in front of you, could you please comment on them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I apologise.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He supported what General Smiljanic, the head of the first administration, said. He took part at the meetings of the collegium from time to time when some important issues were debated. And his question was: What was the alternative to that, to withdraw, or whether this should be discussed at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who is he addressing when he says in the last three lines of the first passage with --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters please have the English version on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to comment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just hold on a second. For some reason the interpreters don't have the English although we do. Can that be rectified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm told we need to occupy the whole screen with the Serb version, so I'm afraid the interpreters will just have to make the most of this. Please continue, Mr. Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He suggested, he asked the Chief of General Staff whether he reserved the right to bring the unit back to this area should the KLA use this territory. And I think it was quite clear what this was all about, because at the negotiations General Clark was told that it should not happen that if and when the army withdraws that after certain time the terrorist forces should take up the positions held by the army previously. General Perisic had stated that quite clearly, and he said that he would reserve this right; and if that should happen, that parts of the military would go back to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: When General Dimitrijevic says this, in addition to what you told everyone that you reserved the right to bring this unit back, does that refer to the negotiations a few days earlier?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that refers to the negotiations that took place a few days earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like us to stick with the same document. The English version is on page 10 and B/C/S version is on page 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Again, this is the intervention by General Ojdanic, is it not, General? And I would like you to tell me, here General Ojdanic expresses a certain dilemma about the concessions made to the army by dint of retaining those three units in the area. What does this refer to?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the gist of it is as follows: These were minimised formations that remained in the area, and it was accepted that these units may remain in the area. This was taken to be some kind of a concession over a certain period of time, to buy some time, and that one point due to some pressure those units would have to be withdrawn. That is why in the debate he advocated the solution for those units to be withdrawn immediately, withdrawn to the barracks immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please comment on what General Perisic had to say at page 11 of the English version. First of all -- at first it seems that General Perisic agrees with General Ojdanic, but then he states certain reasons why those units remained in the area. Could you please tell us something about this.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the then-Chief of General Staff agreed fully with the opinion expressed by General Ojdanic that these units should be withdrawn to the barracks. But he made some comments, expressed his views as to what might follow. Because the units in the area were a certain guarantee of safety for the population and he was afraid that there would be exodus of the Serb population in particular out of fear of terrorist attacks. He gave the example of Dulje where other structures that were deployed there, the MUP units and the population would start to withdraw because they would conclude that the army left them in the lurch, fled, leaving them behind unprotected. So this was a comment that he made. He was afraid of all that, and that is why he insisted that those units should remain deployed in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, now let me ask you, I can see here that the -- that General Perisic ordered that certain degree of combat-readiness should remain, that the units that were there should be at a certain level of combat-readiness.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: The units that withdrew to the barracks should be at the certain level of combat-readiness in case what had been indicated in negotiations with General Clark should occur, that they should be at a certain stand-by for combat-readiness, 24-hour stand-by so that if any new developments occurred that they could be deployed, get out into the area, and carry out tasks, whatever they may be.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, let me ask you something. In 1998 at the time when General Ojdanic was the deputy Chief of General Staff, do you know that he was present or that he was invited to meetings where the situation in Kosovo was discussed, apart from the collegia that you all attended?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, General Ojdanic, the deputy Chief of General Staff, attended the collegia meetings. It is perhaps interesting to note that when the plan Thunder 98 was approved and when those documents were drafted and when the commander of the 3rd Army justified the plan, General Ojdanic, the then-deputy, was absent. I don't know why he didn't attend. It is not up to me to tell you why because I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: He was not a member of the delegation that took part in the negotiations?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: No. General Dimitrijevic, General Panic, myself, and another general was present there; General Ojdanic was not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Do you know if he attended any other meetings? Was he there with you in this control visit in August?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: No. The Chief of General Staff led this team, that was quite a respectable team, and General Ojdanic was not in this team that checked and visited the units in Kosovo and Metohija in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Let us now go back to the unit that was withdrawn from the Podujevo area, that's document 3D785. We now go back to December 1998, that's the time when the Kosovo Verification Mission is already there in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would now like us to look at 3D785, page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, can you tell us what document you have in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: The General Staff, this is a regular, weekly report for the period between the 18th and 24th December, 1998, addressed to the General Staff and also to the liaison team for NATO and OSCE missions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Is this what you received regularly, from the 3rd Army, from the command of the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the team that was on the General Staff, there was the team in the 3rd Army that had to do with liaising with NATO and OSCE teams in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: And we received regular reports from the team that was in the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please show the witness, or rather, we can see it already.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, the first paragraph that says: "On the 19th of December at 0800 hours ..." To cut things short, it describes what happened on the 19th of December. Can you just tell us what units took part in that as far as you were informed?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: This company-strength unit that went out to the training grounds, it was their training grounds where they trained before, Batlava near Podujevo. This was an activity that had to do with training because young soldiers had arrived and they were supposed to carry out certain activities in accordance with the plan and programme so that they could successfully take part in the implementation of tasks. That units went there for a specific purpose, they went out there before, too, it's their training grounds. I know those training grounds, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to be shown, or rather, he can already see it on the same page, paragraph 3 in Serbian, paragraph 4 in English that explains that on the 21st of December there was a particular incident in the same area, in the area of Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how you understood this information of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: We got these -- this information in accordance with the reports that came from subordinate commands every day. The General Staff received the report of the command of the 3rd Army. The unit went to the area in order to train; however, terrorist forces opened fire and, therefore, constituted a threat to safety and security. There is also information to the effect that some persons were wounded and also that the unit partly responded in fire in the area and there were a few such incidents during those several days.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English, page 2, paragraphs 8 and 9. I think that we were able to see that. In the B/C/S version, page 2, paragraphs 2 and 3. There is a description of an incident that occurred on the 24th of December at 9.30 when a soldier from the 15th armour brigade was wounded, and later on yet another incident on the same day when a second lieutenant and a soldier were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like to take you back to the basic document. So tell me the following. I see that in this document after a description of these incidents that under 2 we see incidents where military units were involved and there is a reference to measures that were taken against members of the Army of Yugoslavia who took part in these incidents. What does this refer to, General?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I forgot to mention a few moments ago that the activities of these units -- of this unit was, or rather, the verifiers, the OSCE verifiers were notified of that before. However, what is displayed here that this guard fired two bursts of gun-fire -- is that what you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No, I'm referring to this type of document, these documents that arrived from the missions, these incidents were dealt with specifically, right?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, specifically, especially because they were verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like the witness to be shown the B/C/S text on page 3, and in English also page 3, paragraphs 3 and 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I see that the next item in this report is: "Comments on activities of the Diplomatic Observation Mission ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: No, I'm waiting for -- no, English version is okay. I'm waiting for just last two paragraphs in Serbian page. And the next page on Serbian also.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, it is stated here that the Pristina Corps liaison team informed the mission, and then it says the unit going to the Batlava sector with the objective of carrying out planned exercises envisaged in the unit BO plan and programme. General, is this information that you had in the General Staff in relation to what happened in Podujevo rather the series of incidents that we discussed a few moments ago?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: We had the obligation, or rather, the army had the obligation of reporting to the verifiers company-strength unit movements and above in Kosovo. So the fact that this unit went into the area was reported in detail, including the number of personnel and the equipment used, as well as the direction in which the unit went in order to train. This was an obligation, and as you can see in the report and the notification this was indeed done. The unit from the subordinate command informed the General Staff about this as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: If I read this correctly, two paragraphs down in English it is paragraph 6 on the same page, an explanation was provided as well to the members of the verification mission as to what this was all about.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: An explanation was provided to them. Well, on our part perhaps there was a bit of a misunderstanding, or rather, they asked for something that was not envisaged by the agreement, an elaboration on the actual contents, the targeting plans, and the names of the officers involved. So the officer who was the liaison officer, when he established contact with the members of the mission, in a way he expressed his, well, apologies because there were some minor omissions within the context of that incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, further on page 3, the last paragraph, and page 4, the first paragraph in English. It is stated that as regards to this incident a meeting was held between Generals Loncar and Drewienkiewicz. You received this information, that is to say, information about this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We received this information on contacts between the representatives of the army and the members of the mission in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you to look once again at page 4, paragraph 4 in English; and in Serbian paragraph 3 on page 5. General, the leader of the team of the Pristina Corps tried to explain to the members of the mission the problems, or rather, the situation out in the field. However, at the end of this paragraph it says that what was also said to them was that it was decided that the mentioned units, usually the situation on the ground, would remain in the area of the Batlava airfield even after the 22nd of December. Now, General, tell me, in relation to the previous discussion that General Perisic had during the course of the negotiations or at meetings of the collegium, what was this all about? Why was this unit kept in the area, if you can tell us briefly because we'll be going back to that yet again.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I think that this was one of the indicators to the effect that General Perisic was right when he expressed his doubts as to whether the other side - I'm saying this conditionally, the other side, it was the terrorist forces - whether they would abide by what had been promised; that did not happen. This terrorist activity happened every day. Their objective was to interrupt the road between Podujevo and Pristina, and also various other activities were going on there. And General Perisic said what he said, and the decision made was that this unit should proceed and remain in the area after the 22nd of December, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. We'd be going back to that particular detail yet again. Now I'd like to show you, in the English text pages 5 and 6 and in the B/C/S text it's 7, the very same document. General, until then weekly notifications were provided to the OSCE mission about troop movement and other activities of the Army of Yugoslavia. We saw previously during the course of this trial from various documents that the tendency of the General Staff when headed by General Ojdanic was to have this notification, or rather, this communication with the mission become a daily affair. Can you give us your comments on these proposals that came from the 3rd Army, or rather, their opposition to this proposal not to have daily reporting but to keep weekly reporting?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: The agreement defined that reports or notifications should be submitted weekly in terms of the activities that had taken place during the previous week; however, quite a few elements changed. The requests of the members of the mission varied from day-to-day, if I can put it that way. If there were to be daily notification, well this was just the beginning of the formation of the mission and the liaison's officers had just started working on this, this would have really been an encumbrance for the officers of these units because they were officers of particular units at the same time. Also, there could be abuse of such notification because the teams that were out with the verifiers involved Albanians, too, so there was the possibility of -- well, if the situation were to be presented as to what would happen further on, then there was the danger of this information becoming accessible to the terrorist forces that certainly would have taken certain action vis-a-vis them. However, later on it was noted that this was indispensable and later on an order was issued to have these reports provided on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move on to P928, the collegium of the 30th of December, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, let's go back in time now. The document that you looked at previously was dated the 25th of December, and now we're dealing with a collegium taking place five days after that, on the 30th of December. General, at collegium meetings you often presented information about the situation on the ground and relations with the Kosovo Verification Mission. What were the sources of your information?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: I was appointed leader of the team in the General Staff for relations with the missions on orders issued by the Chief of General Staff. On behalf of the Chief of General Staff I attended sessions of the Federal Commission for relations with the mission; that is to say, in addition to the information that we received on a daily basis on the basis of reports sent by our subordinate commands and the teams for liaising with the missions on the ground and the information that we received at meetings of the Federal Commission as well as other sources. The overall situation was reviewed in that period in the area of Kosovo and Metohija as a whole.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. At this collegium you also spoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we go to pages 10 and 11 B/C/S, or rather, 9 and 10 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: You take the floor after General Dimitrijevic, who stated that there were some efforts or attempts by the terrorist units to spread into urban areas, and he says that this is particularly present in the Podujevo area where the Serbian villages are already abandoned. You take the floor after General Dimitrijevic and could you please tell me what data did you have at that time regarding the situation there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Well, in addition to the detailed analysis presented by General Dimitrijevic at the Federal Commission there was a decision to the effect that under the pressure of the terrorists, not only did the ethnic Serbs leave their homes but that some institutions had to stop functioning. I remember that General [as interpreted] Sainovic chaired the meeting where the justice minister said that some Judges -- that the courts had stopped working, that the judges had left the area saving their families. The institutions of the system were unable to do their job, not to go into anything else that happened. And requests and proposals were made, measures were taken, and at the commission level it was decided that measures should be taken to ensure that the system continues to function for as long as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General -- well, the Judges will have an opportunity to read the whole text of the collegium meeting, but I wanted to ask you, General Bojovic who also made a presentation at the meeting, he is also originally from that area. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, General Bojovic is from a village near Podujevo. He was the advisor of the Chief of General Staff at the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now if we look at page 11 -- 12, could we look at the English and the Serbian version both pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General Bojovic has some first-hand information about the situation there. He goes into quite some detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Serbian I think we have to problem and English. B/C/S page 12, English page -- should be 11. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: General, I don't think you can see it. What did General Bojovic report at the collegium, very briefly?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: Since he's quite familiar with the terrain and in those days he actually went to Kosovo, probably on a mission he received from the Chief of General Staff and he went back through this area along this axis Pristina-Podujevo and further on. He said that he had seen from his car on his way back the trenches next to the very roads that were dug by the terrorist forces. He also said that the -- all the population had left the area, that the population were forcibly gathered, not only ethnic Serbs but also ethnic Albanians who were loyal citizens. And as I noted earlier, there was a threat that very few should stay there and that's what happened. He gave an example. There was a village that had a number of houses, and now only a few people still remain there. So he wanted -- in fact, his opinion was that this unit should remain in that area, but I'm making this comment because there were some opinions that the military should protect the population. But the Chief of General Staff, and I think in particular General Ojdanic based on some experience -- earlier experience, the conclusion was made that the army should not get involved, that this was up to other organs and authorities, primarily the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please look at page 13 in the Serbian version and page 12 I guess in the English version, if we could see it on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: That's the last part of General Bojovic's presentation where he says in the last sentence: "We would have this situation and the political plan or we want to be able to fight terrorism in a legal manner. This is the most severe measures like in any other country," that's the last sentence in General Bojovic's intervention and then we have a comment made by General Dimitrijevic: "This has not been impossible, it is allowed." And then General Bojovic again asks to be allowed to protect the population: "If the army could be there only in a passive role at least to protect villages and the population there." And then we have General Ojdanic's comment. Could you please tell us, how did you understand General Ojdanic's words? We have the experience from Croatia in 1991 when we became embroiled. What does this refer to?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD OBRADOVIC
utterances.text: General Ojdanic in his overall analysis proposed, I think, that the verifiers should get a -- should be asked to secure some communications. This demand that he made for part of the units to remain in the area as a safety element to protect the population, General Ojdanic on the basis of our previous experience and the overall situation was quite categorical. This was not the army's job and the army should not get involved and it did not get involved in those things. I think that he was right.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I know that we have one minute and a half, but I think that we can call it a day now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Visnjic. Mr. Obradovic, we have to conclude for the day at this stage, which means that you have to come back tomorrow to continue to give evidence, that will be at 9.00 tomorrow morning. Meanwhile, it is extremely important that between now and then you have no discussion with anybody at all about the evidence in this case. You can discuss other things with whoever you wish, but one subject you must not discuss with anyone is any of the evidence in the case. Could you now please leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll see you at 9.00 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 5th day of September, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24
